habitat: Loose groups on bare ground, short grassland near dams, airfields, well-grazed farmland and burned areas. Nomadic.
summary: A common localised resident. The adult has a broad black breast-band and a white eyebrow. The immature lacks the breast-band. It sings from a low perch or while fluttering upward, and includes imitations. The Kemp name Capped Wheatear and the code NB were left unchanged.

viewNotes.note: White eyebrow and a broad black breast-band.

calls.description: A variable song with imitations, given from a low prominence or while fluttering upward. The grade A song is from the Karoo Gariep Nature Reserve. The filename is XC596088-Capped Wheatear (2).mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common localised resident and nomadic. Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The grade A song is from the Northern Cape. The Kemp name Capped Wheatear and the code NB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^4=16 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 8–32.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.
